claims.text: The four forms below are parsed as first-class links, and NOT as prose:
claims.why: The actual parsing is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[Note]]``               doc -> doc.  Bare name: matched against the file set; the heading is carried, never verified here.
claims.why: Parsing logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[Note#Heading]]``       the heading is carried, never verified here.
claims.why: Parsing logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[Note|alias]]``         The alias is display text, never part of the target.
claims.why: Parsing logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``![[Note]]`` ``![[a.png]]``  an EMBED (transclusion). Same target resolution, carried with ``embed=True`` -- a caller that renders inline and a caller that draws an edge need to tell the two apart, so the parser does not collapse them.
claims.why: Parsing logic and embed handling not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[code:daedalus/x.py]]``    doc -> CODE.  A SEPARATE relation from doc -> doc, because 'this page documents that file' is not the same claim as 'this page links that page', and a staleness check only makes sense for the former.
claims.why: Parsing logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[type:DSSResult]]``     doc -> TYPE.  PARSED, CARRIED, COUNTED, and DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED: the type layer is being built in parallel, and this module does not import it.  A reference to a resolver that does not exist yet is recorded as deferred, not as unresolved -- 'we did not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' are different claims.
claims.why: Parsing and resolution logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[vault:NAME/path]]`` (cross-vault) is NOT implemented.  It is phase K6 and gated on a separate security review (the ``.md`` egress allow-list and the write-confinement question).  It is recognised only far enough to be counted as deferred and resolved to nothing, so that it can never fall through to the note-name matcher and bind to some same-named local file.
claims.why: Implementation not in this chunk; only constant _NS_VAULT is present.

claims.text: It does not guess.  A link that does not resolve to a file actually present in the file set is DROPPED and COUNTED, never bound to a near-match.  Same rule ``index.py`` already applies to non-Python imports.
claims.why: Resolution logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: It does not break a TIE.  If a wikilink target matches more than one file in the set (``[[note]]`` with both ``a/note.md`` and ``b/note.md`` present, or a relative path that is equally readable as vault-root-relative), NO link is emitted and the occurrence is counted as AMBIGUOUS.
claims.why: Resolution logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: It does not produce a 'distilled' view larger than its input.  ``document_skeleton`` guarantees ``len(result) <= len(text)`` by construction, degrading through a fixed ladder and finally returning the raw document with ``distilled=False`` rather than shipping a lie.
claims.why: Function document_skeleton not in this chunk.

claims.text: It does not run over anything the egress gate has not cleared.  This module never reads a file; callers pass text they have already gated.  See ``slice.py``, where every emitted document goes through the identical ``sensitivity.slice_egress_rule`` call as a source file.
claims.why: Referenced functions not in this chunk; the module has no file reading code visible.

claims.text: Bump when the MEANING of a parse changes (new heading form, different section boundary, changed link resolution). Mirrors ``perfile.ANALYSIS_VERSION``'s role; carried in the index so a stale consumer is detectable rather than silently wrong.
claims.why: The claim refers to perfile.ANALYSIS_VERSION and index, not in this chunk.

claims.text: A document lives in ``index['modules']`` alongside source files -- it genuinely is a file in the repo, it genuinely participates in the link graph, and every consumer that joins on ``modules`` (the DSS hierarchy, the lexical seed, the slice scope boundary) needs it there or the planner stays blind to it, which is the whole defect.
claims.why: Referenced index and consumers not in this chunk.

claims.text: What it must NEVER do is masquerade as code, so its entry carries ``kind: 'document'`` and every code-only consumer filters on exactly this key. Absence means source file, so an index built without documents is byte-identical to before.
claims.why: Referenced consumers not in this chunk.

claims.text: The document analogue of ``parse.CodeUnit`` -- and DELIBERATELY field-compatible with it (``module``/``name``/``line``/``end_line``/``loc``/``source``/``language``) so a document can be handed to code that already accepts units (``graph.build_resolver``, ``slice``'s symbol lookup) without those call sites growing a type switch.

claims.text: ``level`` 0 is the PREAMBLE -- the text before the first heading, i.e. the analogue of module-level code.  A document with no headings at all has exactly one section, which is the honest answer rather than zero.
